formation.title: The Universal Khilafah Restored
formation.text:
After a millennium of dynastic fragmentation, the ummah is one again. Mecca, Medina, Cairo, Damascus, Baghdad, and the seats of the old Umayyad and Abbasid caliphates answer to a single throne. The black standard of the Prophet flies from al-Andalus to Sindh; the call to Friday prayer in every congregational mosque is offered in the name of one Caliph. This is not the work of any one dynasty, Umayyad, Abbasid, Fatimid, Almohad, Mamluk, or Ottoman, but the Rashidun ideal made flesh: the universal community of believers under one banner.

The ulama gather in council. The viziers wait at the gate of the diwan. The world holds its breath. What kind of Khilafah will rise from this restoration?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Caliph in Mecca: restore the Rashidun ideal

modifiers.name: The Caliph in Mecca
modifiers.text: The Caliph rules from the Haramayn, the Two Holy Mosques. Religious authority radiates outward from Mecca and Medina; the founding model of the Rashidun is restored. Sharia is the law, the ulama the only ministers that matter, and the ummah is converted by prestige and example as much as by sword.

effects.name: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

options.text: The Caliph in Baghdad: revive the Abbasid civilization

modifiers.name: The Caliph in Baghdad
modifiers.text: The Khilafah revives the Abbasid imperial civilization: a cosmopolitan synthesis of Arab, Persian, and Turkic learning. Bayt al-Hikmah is rebuilt, the great translation movement resumes, and the Khilafan court welcomes scholars of every faith. The Caliph governs the world from a city of ministries, libraries, and bazaars.

options.text: The Sword and the Sultan: a militant gunpowder Khilafah

modifiers.name: The Sword and the Sultan
modifiers.text: The Khilafah is the world's gunpowder empire. Cannons cast in Cairo, musketeers drilled in Edirne, slave-soldiers raised in Cordoba and the Caucasus march under one banner. The Caliph is warrior-imam: jihad against Christendom, Hindu India, and heterodox sects is permanent state policy.

advances.name: Mujahid Volunteers
advances.text: The volunteer fighter who answers the Caliph's call to defend the Dar al-Islam, drawn from across the ummah without regard to tribe or land.

advances.name: The Ribat Network
advances.text: The frontier garrison-monastery, half fortress and half retreat, holds the marches of the Khilafah. From Aghlabid Tunisia to the Khorasan border, the ribats of the ummah are now a single defensive system.

advances.name: Hajj Logistics
advances.text: The annual pilgrimage to Mecca is codified as a permanent state institution. The Amir al-Hajj commands; the Caliphal treasury underwrites; the wells, forts, and waystations of the Darb Zubayda and the Syrian road are maintained by Caliphal decree.

event.title: The Caliphal Hajj
event.text: Until now, three pilgrim caravans converged on Mecca every year, one from Damascus, one from Cairo, and one from Baghdad, each commanded by a different ruler's officer, each protected by different Bedouin tribes paid different bribes. The new Caliphal decree changes that. From now on, a single Amir al-Hajj, appointed by the Caliph and reporting to no one else, commands all pilgrim caravans. The wells of the Darb Zubayda are repaired; the forts of the Syrian road are regarrisoned; the great Cairo caravan is reorganized. How shall the Caliph project this new institution?

options.text: Make the hajj caravan a march of state

modifiers.name: The Amir al-Hajj
modifiers.text: The annual pilgrimage caravan is now a state institution, commanded by the Amir al-Hajj appointed by the Caliph himself. To shelter the pilgrim is the Caliph's first duty after the defense of the faith.

options.text: Make the pilgrim road a trade road

modifiers.name: The Darb Zubayda
modifiers.text: Wells, cisterns, caravanserais, and waystations stretch from Kufa to Mecca, named for Zubayda bint Ja'far, granddaughter of Caliph al-Mansur. The pilgrim road is also a trade road, and the trade road is also a road of state.

advances.name: The Grand Jami Mosque
advances.text: The Friday-prayer congregational mosque is the visible center of every Khilafan city. From the Umayyad Mosque of Damascus to the Great Mosque of Cordoba, the Khilafah's great jami define the urban fabric of the Islamic world.

advances.name: The Caliphal Diwan
advances.text: The Abbasid bureaucratic apparatus, the diwan al-rasa'il, diwan al-jund, diwan al-kharaj, is restored as the spine of the universal state. Trained scribes administer in standardized Arabic from a single chancery.

advances.name: Universal Sharia
advances.text: The four Sunni madhhabs, Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali, are recognized as one jurisprudence applied across the empire. Where they differ, qadis apply the local madhhab; where they agree, the law is universal.

advances.name: Bayt al-Hikmah Restored
advances.text: Al-Ma'mun's House of Wisdom, the great translation academy that rendered Greek, Sanskrit, and Persian science into Arabic, is rebuilt in Baghdad. Hunayn ibn Ishaq's heirs work in restored chambers; the manuscripts the Mongols destroyed are recopied from surviving exemplars in Cordoba, Cairo, and Bukhara.

event.title: The House of Wisdom Reopens
event.text: Two centuries after Hulegu's Mongols hurled the books of Bayt al-Hikmah into the Tigris, a new House of Wisdom rises in Baghdad's restored quarter. Translators in Greek, Syriac, Persian, and Sanskrit work alongside Arab philosophers; al-Ma'mun's old vision is renewed. Already manuscripts of Galen, Aristotle, and Aryabhata are circulating again, copied in elegant naskh in dozens of madrasahs from Fez to Samarkand. The Caliph stands beside the chief translator and asks: what kind of knowledge shall we honor first?

options.text: Translate every science of the world

modifiers.name: The Translation Movement
modifiers.text: Greek, Sanskrit, Persian, and Syriac texts are systematically rendered into Arabic. Hunayn ibn Ishaq's heirs work in the new Bayt al-Hikmah, and the science of three civilizations passes into a single language.

options.text: Restore the philosophical tradition

modifiers.name: The Falsafa Revival
modifiers.text: Ibn Sina, al-Farabi, and Ibn Rushd are read again in every Khilafan court. Islamic philosophy reclaims its place between revelation and reason; the synthesis that produced Aquinas is renewed in its own homeland.

advances.name: The Ghulam Corps
advances.text: The slave-soldier mounted guard, perfected under al-Mu'tasim and refined by every Islamic dynasty since, is the Caliph's personal cavalry. The ghulam answer to the throne alone, not to tribe or province.

event.title: The Caliphal Ghulam
event.text: The slave-soldier system, once the curse of the late Abbasids when ghilman became kingmakers in Samarra, is now the Khilafah's most reliable institution. Boys from the Caucasus, the Sudan, and the Balkans are bought, converted, schooled, drilled, and bound to the Caliph alone. They have no kin to favor and no homeland to flee to. As the corps grows, the Caliph must decide what work it shall do.

options.text: Deploy the ghulam as the Caliph's guard

modifiers.name: The Caliphal Ghulam Guard
modifiers.text: Slave-soldiers raised from childhood in the Caliph's household form an elite mounted guard, devoted only to the throne. Their loyalty is to the Caliph alone, not to any tribe, dynasty, or province.

options.text: Send the best as provincial governors

modifiers.name: Ghulam Governors
modifiers.text: The most able ghulam are sent out as provincial commanders and governors. They have no local kin to favor, no native hereditary claim, only their oath to the Caliph who raised them.

advances.name: The Caliphal Galley
advances.text: The Mediterranean fleets of Cordoba, Tunis, Alexandria, and Constantinople are unified into a single Caliphal navy. The Levantine, Maghrebi, and Andalusi shipbuilding traditions cross-fertilize.

advances.name: The Caliphal Dirham
advances.text: Abd al-Malik's silver dirham of 696 is restored as the universal coinage. Local minting is regulated; weights are standardized; the Khilafan dirham becomes the world's reserve currency.

event.title: The Khilafan Dirham
event.text: Since the days of Abd al-Malik, the dirham has been the silver currency of the Islamic world, and since the day after that, every local ruler has debased it for his own benefit. The Khilafan reform forbids local minting, fixes the dirham's weight and silver content by Caliphal decree, and stamps the new coins from a few central mints under direct supervision. Merchants from Granada to Bengal will trust this coinage. What is the Khilafah's monetary policy?

options.text: A pure silver standard, Caliphal coinage only

modifiers.name: The Silver Dirham Standard
modifiers.text: A single weight of silver, struck in mints from Cordoba to Bukhara, is accepted in every market of the Khilafah. Currency manipulation by local rulers ends; the Caliphal dirham is the world's standard.

options.text: Open the Caliphal mints, increase the supply

modifiers.name: The Caliphal Mints
modifiers.text: Silver from the Hindu Kush, Anatolia, and the Sahel flows into Caliphal mints; gold from West Africa and Egypt is struck into the Khilafan dinar. The treasury overflows.

advances.name: The Universal Madrasah
advances.text: The Nizamiyya, the Mustansiriyya, al-Azhar, the Qarawiyyin, the great madrasahs of Bukhara and Samarkand and Cordoba teach a unified Khilafan curriculum. A scholar trained in Fez can teach in Lahore.

event.title: The Council of the Ulama
event.text: For the first time since the early Abbasids, the chief jurists of the four Sunni madhhabs sit in council together. The Hanafi mufti of Constantinople, the Shafi'i sheikh of al-Azhar, the Maliki imam of the Qarawiyyin, and the Hanbali alim of Mecca debate the boundaries of what is permitted, what is forbidden, and what is left to discretion. The Caliph presides but does not vote. What shall come of this synod?

options.text: Affirm orthodoxy through unity

modifiers.name: The Concord of the Ulama
modifiers.text: The four Sunni madhhabs: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali, confer in council under the Caliph's patronage. Differences remain, but the schools recognize one another and one supreme authority above them all.

options.text: Forge a new universal jurisprudence

modifiers.name: The Madhhab Synthesis
modifiers.text: A new generation of jurists trained in all four madhhabs reasons across them, producing a synthetic fiqh suitable for an empire that spans Berber, Arab, Persian, Turkic, and Indian Muslims.

advances.name: The Tariqas Unified
advances.text: The Sufi orders, Naqshbandi, Qadiriyya, Mevlevi, Bektashi, Chishti, Shadhili, are brought under Caliphal patronage. The Caliph endorses no single tariqa, but every order accepts him as Amir al-Mu'minin.

event.title: The Tariqas Unite
event.text: Until this council, every Sufi order, the Naqshbandi, the Qadiriyya, the Mevlevi, the Bektashi, the Chishti, the Shadhili, has answered to its own silsila of masters and disciples, sometimes orthodox, sometimes heterodox, often both. Now the chief sheikhs of the great orders gather under Caliphal patronage. The Caliph proposes: there is no one Sufi path, but there is one Khilafah, and every order shall serve it. The orders accept. The question is which Sufism shall flourish.

options.text: Patronize the sober and orthodox orders

modifiers.name: The Sober Path
modifiers.text: The Naqshbandi and Qadiriyya orders win Caliphal favor: their sober, scholarly Sufism reinforces orthodoxy rather than challenging it. Mystical devotion strengthens the state.

options.text: Patronize the ecstatic and converting orders

modifiers.name: The Ecstatic Path
modifiers.text: The Mevlevi, Bektashi, and Chishti orders flourish under Caliphal patronage. Music, poetry, and dance become tools of universal Islamic conversion across cultural lines.

advances.name: Post-Mongol Restoration
advances.text: The damage of the Mongol century, sacked cities, ruined irrigation, lost manuscripts, decimated populations, is systematically repaired. The Khilafah's engineers and bureaucrats undo what Hulegu, Timur, and the Black Death together had wrought.

event.title: Baghdad Rises Again
event.text: On the banks of the Tigris, masons lay the foundations of a new caliphal palace where the Round City of al-Mansur once stood. The new madrasahs go up next: the Mustansiriyya is rebuilt, then the Nizamiyya. Engineers restore the irrigation canals the Mongols broke. The trauma of 1258, when the Tigris ran black with the ink of drowned books and red with the blood of the last Abbasid Caliph, is finally being healed by ordinary craftsmanship. Where shall the Khilafah's effort be focused?

options.text: Rebuild Baghdad as the world's greatest city

modifiers.name: Baghdad Reborn
modifiers.text: The horror of 1258, when Hulegu's Mongols sacked Baghdad and threw the libraries of the Caliphs into the Tigris, is reversed at last. The City of Peace is rebuilt; the Round City is replanned; the Tigris reflects domes and minarets again.

options.text: Restore every ruined province of the ummah

modifiers.name: Dar al-Islam Unbroken
modifiers.text: The fragmentation of the post-Mongol world is healed. Every Sunni community, from Granada to the Indus, knows it stands within a single Dar al-Islam, defended by a single Caliph.

advances.name: The Gunpowder Caliphate
advances.text: Ottoman bombards, Mamluk arquebuses, and Mughal matchlocks are fused into a single Khilafan doctrine of gunpowder warfare. The Caliphal foundries cast cannon by a single specification from Cairo to Lahore.

event.title: The Gunpowder Caliphate
event.text: Mehmed's bombards once felled the walls of Constantinople. Selim's musketeers swept the Mamluks at Marj Dabiq. Babur's gunners broke the Lodis at Panipat. Now those traditions, Ottoman, Mamluk, Mughal, all bend the knee to one Caliph and merge into one doctrine of war. The Topkapi master gunners drill in Aleppo; the Mughal arquebusiers train in Cairo; the foundries of Edirne, Alexandria, and Lahore cast cannon to a single specification. How shall the new doctrine be applied?

options.text: The Caliphal artillery train

modifiers.name: The Caliphal Artillery Park
modifiers.text: Great siege bombards cast in Cairo, mortars in Edirne, and field guns from the foundries of Constantinople move under one Caliphal command. No fortress in the world is beyond reach.

options.text: The musket-armed jihad

modifiers.name: The Jihad of the Gun
modifiers.text: Janissary corps, Mamluk arquebusiers, and Mughal matchlockmen are unified into a single doctrine: the gunpowder jihad. The Khilafah's enemies face concentrated firepower under religious motivation.

effects.name: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

advances.name: Universal Iqta
advances.text: The land-grant systems of the Abbasids (iqta), Mamluks (iqta), Seljuks-Ottomans (timar), and Mughals (jagir) are unified into a single tenure: hold land for service, lose land for failure to serve.

event.title: The Universal Diwan
event.text: The Abbasid iqta, the Mamluk iqta, the Seljuk-Ottoman timar, the Mughal jagir, all four were the same idea in different languages: a soldier holds land from the state and serves the state in war. The Khilafan grand vizier proposes that they be unified, codified, and rationalized into a single tenure system, manageable from a single ledger in the Central Diwan. The reform faces resistance from established holders. How shall it be implemented?

options.text: Centralize tax assessment in the Diwan

modifiers.name: The Central Diwan
modifiers.text: Tax registers from Lisbon to Lahore are unified. The Caliphal diwan keeps a single ledger for the whole world, and from that ledger the world is governed.

options.text: Empower local timariots in return for service

modifiers.name: Provincial Timariots
modifiers.text: Sipahi cavalry, iqta-holders, and Mamluk land-grantees are unified under a single tenure system: serve the Caliph in war, hold land in return. Provincial cavalry levies multiply across the empire.

advances.name: The Two Oceans Fleet
advances.text: The Mediterranean fleet at Constantinople and Alexandria and the Indian Ocean fleet at Suez and Aden are placed under unified Caliphal command. From Gibraltar to Malacca, one Kapudan Pasha commands.

event.title: Two Oceans, One Banner
event.text: The fleet at Alexandria carries the green Caliphal banner; so does the dockyard at Suez, the squadron at Aden, the patrol at Hormuz, the corsair fleet of the Maghreb, and the Ottoman Kapudan-i Derya's ships of the line. For the first time since the Fatimids, the Indian Ocean and the Mediterranean are commanded together. The Portuguese intrusion can be answered with a coordinated reply. Where shall the Khilafah strike first?

options.text: Drive the Franks from the Indian Ocean

modifiers.name: Indian Ocean Supremacy
modifiers.text: From Aden to Calicut, from Mombasa to Malacca, the Caliphal banner rules the monsoon trade. The Portuguese intrusion is rolled back; the spice trade flows once more under Khilafan protection.

options.text: Master the Mediterranean as a Khilafan lake

modifiers.name: Mediterranean Thalassocracy
modifiers.text: The fleet at Alexandria, the dockyards of the Golden Horn, and the corsair captains of the Maghreb answer to one Kapudan Pasha. The Mediterranean becomes a Khilafan lake.

advances.name: The Arabic Printing Press
advances.text: The technical problem of cursive Arabic typesetting is at last solved. Printed Qur'ans, hadith collections, legal manuals, and scientific treatises spread literacy at unprecedented speed.

event.title: Arabic Type
event.text: After two centuries of resistance from the calligraphers' guilds, the first Arabic-script printing press is licensed in Constantinople, then Cairo, then Baghdad, then Cordoba. The technical problem of cursive Arabic, with its letters changing shape by position, has at last been solved by Khilafan typographers. Books that once cost a year's wages now cost weeks. The Caliph must decide what shall flow first from the new presses.

options.text: Print the Qur'an for every village mosque

modifiers.name: The Qur'anic Press
modifiers.text: Arabic typesetting, long resisted by calligraphers, is finally mastered. Printed Qur'ans, hadith collections, and devotional manuals reach every village mosque.

options.text: Print the sciences for every madrasah

modifiers.name: The Scientific Press
modifiers.text: Treatises on astronomy, medicine, mathematics, and law come off Khilafan presses by the thousand. Scientific knowledge propagates faster than ever in Islamic history.

advances.name: Caliphal Corsairs
advances.text: The Barbary corsairs, the Levantine privateers, and the Adeni raiders all sail under Caliphal letters of marque. The Khilafah's enemies cannot move a merchantman without paying.

advances.name: Sharif Legitimacy
advances.text: The Caliph's descent from the Prophet's family is publicly affirmed by every Sharif in Mecca, Medina, and Hadramawt. The legitimacy of the Khilafah is bound to the bloodline of the Prophet himself.

advances.name: The Caliphal Slave Corps
advances.text: The janissary system of the Ottomans, the Mamluk Bahri and Burji, the Persian ghulam: all are absorbed into a single Caliphal slave-corps numbering tens of thousands. They are the world's first standing professional army.

advances.name: The Tofangchi Corps
advances.text: The Persian-Mughal tofangchi musketeer is unified with the Mamluk arquebusier and the Ottoman tüfekçi into a single Caliphal light infantry tradition: matchlock and discipline.

advances.name: The Oceanic Galleon
advances.text: Combining Indian Ocean dhow rigging with Iberian galleon construction, the Khilafan oceanic galleon carries Caliphal trade and Caliphal arms across both oceans.

advances.name: The Universal Court
advances.text: The Abbasid divani court of Baghdad, the Topkapi protocol of the Ottomans, the Mughal darbar, all are absorbed into a single Khilafan court ceremonial, projecting universal sovereignty.

advances.name: Pan-Sunni Authority
advances.text: The Caliph is recognized as imam of all four Sunni madhhabs simultaneously. His Friday khutba is read in every congregational mosque from Granada to Sumatra.

advances.name: Imperial Integration
advances.text: Berber, Arab, Egyptian, Levantine, Anatolian, Persian, Turkic, Indian, and Andalusi Muslims all consider themselves subjects of one Khilafah first, members of their local communities second.

advances.name: Caliphal Absolutism
advances.text: The Caliph is no longer first among equals among the local rulers of the Sunni world; he is the absolute sovereign over a single integrated state stretching across three continents.

advances.name: The Modern Caliphal Navy
advances.text: Frigates and ships-of-the-line, dockyards modeled on the best Iberian and Atlantic practice, professional captains drawn from a single Khilafan academy: the navy modernizes without losing its Mediterranean and monsoon character.

advances.name: The Caliphal Bank
advances.text: A Khilafan credit network using sakk (cheques), suftaja (bills of exchange), and the new institutional lending of the post-Reformation world ties Cairo, Damascus, Baghdad, Constantinople, Aleppo, and Cordoba into a single financial system.

advances.name: The Caliphal Scientific Revolution
advances.text: The Khilafah's astronomers, mathematicians, physicians, and chemists, working from Mecca to Cordoba in a single Arabic scientific community, drive a Khilafan parallel to the European scientific revolution.

advances.name: Universal Legitimacy
advances.text: Christian and Hindu states accept the Khilafah's diplomatic precedence; the rulers of Spain, France, the Holy Roman Empire, and the Hindu kingdoms address the Caliph as a peer or superior. The Khilafah is the world's senior power.

advances.name: The Caliphal Tanzimat
advances.text: Codified law, conscript armies, salaried officials, technical schools, telegraphs, railways: the Khilafah modernizes from above, drawing on European models without surrendering its Islamic character.

event.title: The Caliphal Tanzimat
event.text: European steam ships dock at Khilafan ports. European telegraph lines reach Khilafan capitals. European armies, smaller than the Caliph's by a factor of ten, defeat his frontier forces by drill and rifled musket. Reform is no longer optional. The grand vizier presents two memoranda: one calling for codified law, conscript armies, technical schools, salaried officials, and an industrial economy; the other calling for a return to the way of the salaf, a stripping-away of accretions, a militant orthodox revival. The Caliph hears both and must choose.

options.text: Modernize from above; adopt what works

modifiers.name: The Caliphal Tanzimat
modifiers.text: Codified law, conscript armies, salaried officials, technical schools, telegraphs, and railways: the Khilafah modernizes from above, drawing on European models without surrendering Islamic identity.

options.text: Return to the way of the pious ancestors

modifiers.name: The Salafi Revival
modifiers.text: A return to the way of the salaf al-salih, the pious ancestors. The accretions of centuries are stripped away; a leaner, harder, more militant Sunni orthodoxy emerges, rejecting both Sufi heterodoxy and European reform.

advances.name: The Modern Caliphal Army
advances.text: Conscription replaces the levy and the slave-corps. Rifled muskets replace matchlocks. Drilled battalions replace sipahi cavalry. The Nizami Jadid is the model army of the late Khilafah.

advances.name: The Steam Navy
advances.text: Steam frigates and ironclads built in Khilafan dockyards from Constantinople to Bombay carry the green banner into the age of industrial naval warfare.

advances.name: The Pan-Islamic Congress
advances.text: A modern diplomatic institution, the Caliphal Congress speaks for the ummah at the Concert of Powers. Where the European empires send foreign ministers, the Khilafah sends a single voice for the global Islamic community.

advances.name: The Industrial Khilafah
advances.text: Cotton mills in Egypt, foundries in Anatolia, shipyards in Suez, mechanized looms in Damascus, and railroad networks linking Cairo, Baghdad, and Lahore: the Khilafah industrializes on its own terms.

destiny.name: The Universal Caliph Crowned
destiny.text: The first khutba is read from a thousand minbars in the name of one Caliph. From al-Andalus to Sindh, the world recognizes a single sovereign of the believers. The path the Khilafah takes from this hour will shape every age that follows.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Universal Caliph Crowned
event.text: The bay'ah is sworn before a million witnesses. From the steps of the Kaaba to the Topkapi gate, from the Qarawiyyin to the Lahore Fort, every qadi, sheikh, sayyid, sharif, and amir of the Sunni world places his hand on the Caliph's and pledges obedience. The Caliph is no longer one ruler among many; he is the Amir al-Mu'minin in fact, not merely in title. A new age begins.

options.text: May the Khilafah endure forever

destiny.name: Mastery of the Two Seas
destiny.text: Secure both the Bab al-Mandab and the Strait of Hormuz. Aden and Hormuz are the gates of the monsoon trade; control of both means the Khilafah's flag commands every dhow from Sofala to Canton. The Caliphal treasury draws on the wealth of the Indian Ocean for the first time since the Fatimid sea routes.

Own 'Adan, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Two Seas Are Ours
event.text: The Caliphal admiral at Aden reports: the Bab al-Mandab is closed to all flags but the green. The Caliphal admiral at Hormuz reports: the Strait is patrolled by Khilafan dhows and warships, no Frankish ship passes without paying. The two gates of the monsoon are turned at last; the Indian Ocean is once more a Muslim sea.

options.text: Set sail for the Malabar

destiny.name: The Spice Crescent
destiny.text: Hold Calicut and Goa, the Malabar entrepots, and bring the silk and pepper trades into Khilafan markets. The crescent of Indian Ocean ports stretching from Aden to Cochin becomes a single mercantile system, the spice trade an instrument of Caliphal policy.

Own Goa, or a subject owns it
A market the country is in

event.title: The Spice Crescent
event.text: Calicut and Goa stand under the Caliphal banner. The Zamorin sends gifts; the old Bahmani sultans pay tribute; the Portuguese Estado da India is reduced to a few coastal forts and a memory. The Malabar pepper, the Coromandel cotton, and the Bengali silk all flow now into Khilafan factor-houses. The Caliph's grand vizier presents two policies for the new commerce.

options.text: Cooperative trade with the monsoon powers

modifiers.name: The Monsoon Compact
modifiers.text: The Caliphate trades with the monsoon powers as partners, not subjects. Khilafan factor-houses appear in Calicut, Cochin, Acheen, Brunei. Indian and Malay merchants are accepted in the Caliphal court; Arabic, Persian, and Tamil traders share warehouses; the Indian Ocean becomes a multinational Khilafan free trade zone.

options.text: Forceful monopoly: Caliphal goods only

modifiers.name: The Pepper Monopoly
modifiers.text: Pepper, cloves, and nutmeg are reserved for the Caliphal pass. Foreign traders without Khilafan licenses are seized; the spice trade becomes a strict royal monopoly. The treasury fattens and the corsairs grow rich, but the diplomatic corps is reduced as foreign embassies depart in protest.

destiny.name: The Caliphate of the Two Oceans
destiny.text: Take Mombasa, Malacca, and Aceh. The Khilafah's banner now flies on both shores of the Indian Ocean and at the gateway to the South China Sea. The Bayt al-Hikmah is rebuilt on a scale to match the empire: a global institution of learning that synthesizes the knowledge of three civilizations.

Own Malacca, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Two Oceans Speak Arabic
event.text: Mombasa, Malacca, Aceh. The Swahili coast, the Strait of Malacca, the northern tip of Sumatra. The Khilafah holds the entry and the exit and every island in between. From the Arabian Peninsula to the Spice Islands, no merchant moves but with a Caliphal pass; no fleet sails but with the green banner. The world's oceans are bilingual: Arabic and silence. What shall be the great work of this hour?

options.text: An empire of universal commerce

modifiers.name: Oceanic Civilization
modifiers.text: The Khilafah is no longer a continental empire with a navy; it is a maritime civilization in its own right. Arabic-speaking trading communities flourish from Mombasa to Manila; Khilafan exploration fleets push out beyond the monsoon into the open Pacific; the spice routes are no longer routes but the spine of a hemispheric polity.

options.text: An empire of universal learning

modifiers.name: The Pan-Islamic University Network
modifiers.text: The Bayt al-Hikmah is no longer one library but a network: branch universities in Cordoba, Cairo, Baghdad, Bukhara, Lahore, and Aceh, all teaching the unified Khilafan curriculum, all sharing manuscripts via Caliphal couriers. The Christian and Hindu worlds resent the cultural dominance, but the Khilafah's scholars span continents.

destiny.name: The Two Cities of the Franks
destiny.text: Conquer Rome and Vienna. The two great Frankish capitals fall to the Caliphal sword: the See of Saint Peter and the gate of central Europe. Ribats are raised in ten places to hold the marches behind the advance. The Christian empires of the Latins are broken at their heart; jihad against Christendom is no longer a frontier action but a planetary fact.

event.title: Rome and Vienna Fall
event.text: The Pope flees toward Avignon; the Emperor retreats beyond the Alps. The minarets rise on the Seven Hills; the call to prayer echoes from the Stephansdom. The Latin Christendom that has resisted the Khilafah for nine centuries is broken at its capitals. The Caliphal armies march onward; the work is not yet done.

options.text: On to Paris and Madrid

destiny.name: The Hammer of Christendom and India
destiny.text: Hold Kataka, Vijayanagar and Toledo. The Gajapati kings of Odisha, whose coast no sultan of Delhi or Bengal could take, are brought under direct Caliphal rule; the southern Hindu power of Vijayanagar is broken in turn, and the old capital of Castile is taken in the west. Two thousand ducats are laid by. East and West fall to one hammer.

event.title: The Hammer Falls East and West
event.text: Kataka is taken: the throne of the Gajapati kings, which no sultan of Delhi could seize, answers to the Khilafah. Vijayanagar is broken: the great Hindu southern empire is reduced to ash. India answers to one Caliph. In the same hour, the last Aragonese and Castilian holdouts fall, and the Mediterranean is bracketed by Khilafan banners. The next campaign begins. Where shall the sword fall?

options.text: The eastern jihad: India must be Islamic

modifiers.name: The Hindu Jihad
modifiers.text: The eastern campaign continues. The Khilafan armies push beyond Delhi into the Deccan, the Ganges valley, and the southern coasts. The fortresses of the Hindu kingdoms fall one by one to the unified Khilafan siege train; the great temple cities of the south submit or are destroyed.

effects.name: Damage Done versus Heathens in Battle

options.text: The western reconquest: Iberia and Italy must be Islamic

modifiers.name: The Andalusi Reconquista
modifiers.text: The wound of 1492 is reversed. Granada is restored, then Toledo, then the Italian peninsula bends. The Christian crusader orders mount a final response, and the antagonism of the Latin world rises to its peak, but the Caliphal banners advance regardless.

effects.name: Damage Done versus Heretics in Battle

destiny.name: The World Submits
destiny.text: Take Paris, Venice, and Madrid. The three capitals of Frankish power, Capet, Doge, and Habsburg, fall to the Caliphal armies, and ribats stand in twenty-five places across the conquests. The Imperial Foundry is built to commemorate the conquest: a universal armory casting the cannon of every conquest from Cordoba to Lahore to one specification.

event.title: The World Submits
event.text: Paris, Venice, Madrid. The Capets, the Doge, the Habsburgs, all three thrones fall in a single decade. The Mediterranean is a Khilafan lake; the Atlantic coast is a Khilafan frontier; the Caliphal flag flies from Lisbon to Lahore. No power on earth resists. The grand vizier submits two memoranda for the new universal order.

options.text: The Khilafah perfects the universal sword

modifiers.name: The Universal Sword
modifiers.text: Heretic Christendom and heathen India both lie open to the Caliphal armies. The sipahi cavalry, the janissary corps, the Mughal artillery train, and the Andalusi reconquerors campaign in coordinated theaters. No power on earth fields a force that can stop them in open battle.

options.text: The Khilafah perfects the universal state

modifiers.name: The Caliphal Imperium
modifiers.text: The conquered world is administered. Forts rise in every conquered province; the imperial road network reaches from Lisbon to Lahore; Caliphal diplomatic missions are dispatched to every remaining throne. The Khilafah is not just an army but a state, the world's first and only universal state.

units.name: Mujahid Volunteers
units.text: Volunteer infantry from across the ummah, motivated by faith and the Caliph's call. Highly motivated but lightly armored.

units.name: Ghulam Cavalry
units.text: The Caliph's slave-soldier mounted guard, raised from childhood and bound to the throne alone. Elite shock cavalry in the Yarmuk tradition.

units.name: Caliphal Galley
units.text: Mediterranean galley combining Andalusi, Maghrebi, Egyptian, and Levantine shipbuilding traditions. The standard warship of the unified Khilafan Mediterranean fleet.

units.name: Caliphal Galleon
units.text: Heavy ocean-going warship combining Iberian galleon design with Indian Ocean rigging, suited equally to Mediterranean broadside and monsoon-season trade protection.

units.name: Caliphal Slave Corps
units.text: Janissary-equivalent slave infantry: drilled, drilled again, fed by the Caliphal kitchen, paid by the Caliphal treasury, and bound to the Caliph alone.

units.name: Tofangchi Musketeers
units.text: Light musketeer skirmishers in the Persian-Mughal tradition, armed with matchlocks and trained to harry larger formations.

units.name: Oceanic Galleon
units.text: The large broadside warship of the Two Oceans Fleet, designed for sustained naval operations across both the Mediterranean and the Indian Ocean.

units.name: Caliphal Frigate
units.text: Modernized fast warship combining the best Iberian and Ottoman naval traditions, the workhorse of the absolutist-era Caliphal navy.

units.name: Nizami Jadid
units.text: The New Order army: conscript infantry drilled in European fashion but serving under the Khilafan flag. Rifled musket, modern uniform, professional officer corps.

units.name: Caliphal Steam Frigate
units.text: Steam-powered modern warship built in the dockyards of Suez, Constantinople, and Bombay, projecting Khilafan naval power into the industrial age.

buildings.name: Ribat
buildings.text: Frontier garrison-monastery housing volunteer fighters and ascetics on the marches of the Khilafah. Half fortress, half religious retreat.

buildings.name: Hajj Caravanserai
buildings.text: Walled compound with stables, water cisterns, and shaded sleeping quarters along the pilgrim road. Maintained by Caliphal decree, it serves both pilgrims and merchant caravans.

buildings.name: Grand Jami Mosque
buildings.text: The great Friday-prayer congregational mosque, the visible heart of every Khilafan city. The minbar from which the Caliph's khutba is delivered.

buildings.name: Caliphal Diwan
buildings.text: The chancery and finance ministry of the Khilafah, with its trained scribes, sealed registers, and standardized Arabic protocols.

buildings.name: Bayt al-Hikmah
buildings.text: House of Wisdom: a great library, translation academy, and observatory combined. Greek, Sanskrit, Persian, and Syriac manuscripts are rendered into Arabic; new science is generated in dialogue with translated tradition.

buildings.name: Caliphal Mint
buildings.text: Mint of the silver dirham and gold dinar, struck to Caliphal weight specifications and accepted in every market of the Khilafah.

buildings.name: Universal Madrasah
buildings.text: Religious-academic college teaching the unified Khilafan curriculum. A scholar trained in Fez can teach in Bukhara; a graduate of al-Azhar serves in Lahore.

buildings.name: Sufi Khanqah
buildings.text: Sufi lodge housing a tariqa fraternity. The brothers conduct dhikr, host travelers, support converts, and bind the local community to the universal Caliphal Sufi network.

buildings.name: Caliphal Bank
buildings.text: Major credit institution offering sakk, suftaja, and modern institutional lending across the pan-Khilafan financial network.

buildings.name: Bayt al-Hikmah Restored
buildings.text: The second House of Wisdom: a global institution of translation, library, observatory, and university combined. The first Bayt al-Hikmah was Baghdad's; this one is the world's. Manuscripts arrive from Mombasa and Malacca alongside those from Cordoba and Bukhara, all rendered into Arabic by a permanent staff of translators.
buildings.unlocked_by: The Caliphate of the Two Oceans

buildings.name: Caliphal Imperial Foundry
buildings.text: The universal armory of the Khilafah. Cannon foundries from Cairo, Edirne, Lahore, and Cordoba are unified into a single production system; standardized bombards, mortars, field guns, and matchlocks are cast to one specification and shipped to every Caliphal arsenal.

list.name: Dar al-'Adl
list.text: The House of Justice. Nur al-Din built the first in Damascus around 1163 and sat in it twice a week to hear complaints against his own officers. Baybars built another below the citadel of Cairo in the 1260s, and heard petitions there with the chief judges of the four schools beside him. In the restored Caliphate anyone may hand in a written petition, from any province, against any governor or tax farmer, and the answer goes back in the Caliph's name.

conditions.text: Sunnism religion

list.name: Diwan al-Zimam
list.text: The bureau of control. The Abbasid Caliph al-Mahdi, who reigned from 775 to 785, set an audit office beside every bureau of state and a central one above them all to check their books. A Caliphate that reaches from al-Andalus to the Indus cannot keep its revenue in one treasury. Every province keeps its own, and the Zimam in the capital reads each ledger, sets what was assessed against what arrived, and sends its clerks to ask about the difference.

conditions.text: Sunnism religion

list.name: Pan-Islamic Ulama Council
list.text: The unification of the four orthodox Sunni madhhabs (Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali) under joint Caliphal patronage, modeled on the Mamluk practice of seating a chief qadi from each madhhab and extended to imperial scale. Coordinated fatwas, harmonized procedure, and a transregional clerical training corps anchored on al-Azhar. The price of orthodox consolidation is paid by the dhimmi communities whose old legal pluralism narrows under sustained Sunni pressure.

conditions.text: Sunnism religion

list.name: Kiswa of the Kaaba
list.text: Whoever holds Mecca and Medina clothes the Kaaba. Each year a new covering, the kiswa, travels with the pilgrimage, a custom the Abbasid Caliph al-Mahdi made annual. From 1349 the Mamluk sultans paid for it out of the rents of three Egyptian villages set aside for nothing else. With the cloth go gifts for the sharifs and the poor of the two cities. The caravans of Egypt, Syria, Iraq and Yemen meet at Mecca each year under their rulers' banners. Any ruler can send pilgrims. The covering is the Caliph's alone.

Owns Madīna

list.name: Bayt al-Hikmah Network
list.text: The universal-scale revival of the Abbasid House of Wisdom, founded under al-Ma'mun in Baghdad around 830. A federation of translation bureaus and observatories yokes the Toledo, Cordoba, Cairo, Damascus, Baghdad, Isfahan, and Samarkand academies into a single transregional scholarly apparatus. Greek, Sanskrit, Persian, and Latin works flow through a coordinated translation pipeline. The orthodox jurists who follow al-Ghazali in mistrusting falsafa as rationalist intrusion view the network with suspicion.
